event_confirmation: SMFG's own English IR calendar (https://www.smfg.co.jp/english/investor/calendar/, read 2026-11-12) lists 'Nov. 13: Announcement of 6-month results (ended Sep. 30, 2026)', with the results presentation on Nov. 19. kabuyoho's header also reads 'next release 2026/11/13'. A Tokyo release on 13 Nov JST, whether at 15:00 inside the TSE session or after the 15:30 close, falls between the 12 Nov US close and the 13 Nov US open (15:00 JST is 01:00 ET), so the window contains the event. The exact release minute was not confirmed.
conviction_note: abs_move 3.5 comes from the ADR's reactions to its last three interim releases, rebuilt from Yahoo daily closes (+5.6% on 2023-11-14, +2.9% on 2024-11-14, +5.5% on 2025-11-14; each interim brought a raised guide and, in 2025, a ¥150bn buyback). The other prints were small (-1.4% Q3 Jan 2026, +1.0% FY May 2026, +0.4% Q1 Jul 2026). p_up is 60: three of the company's own numbers point to a raise from ¥1.7tn and a buyback (30% progress in Q1, a BOJ hike above the plan's rate assumption, credit cost running below plan), but the consensus already sits about 9% above the guide (~¥1.85tn) and the Q1 beat was not bought, so the raise is expected. impact_sum (+1.65) is larger than the scaled +0.7 because each finding is sized on its own and most of them land on the one guide-raise event the market already leans toward.
bar: Company FY3/27 net income guide ¥1.70tn, unchanged at Q1 (SMFG 1Q FY3/27 overview, https://www.smfg.co.jp/english/investor/financial/latest_statement/2027_3/2027_1q_e03.pdf, 2026-07-31). The bar the stock trades against is the street FY consensus. Chartmill gives about ¥1.851tn from 15 analysts as of 2026-10-24 (snippet only, page 403: https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/SMFG/estimates). kabuyoho gives a FY ordinary-profit consensus of about ¥2.62tn against the ¥2.39tn guide (+9.6%), which is consistent with that net figure, though the mobile table is scrambled (https://kabuyoho.jp/sp/report?bcode=8316). In May the Bloomberg consensus was ¥1.761tn (https://www.bloomberg.com/jp/news/articles/2026-05-13/TEY037KK3NY900). No sourced 1H consensus. print_vs_bar_pct is the expected revised FY guide (~¥1.88-1.90tn) against ~¥1.85tn. The consensus rests on snippets, so the sizes are kept moderate.
positioning_check: Short interest is negligible: about 8.6m ADRs short, ~0.14% of float, 4.9 days to cover as of 2026-08-19, and 8,633,699 shares with 4.58 DTC at the 2026-05-29 settlement (https://equibles.com/stocks/smfg/short-interest). No October settlement was found. This is not a crowded short. Options are unusable: the baseline marks the chain unusable_chain, the ATM spread is 160% of mid, no 25-delta skew, put/call OI 0.88 on only 663 contracts, so there is no directional statement from the option market. Tape: the ADR is +4.0% over 5 days and -1.37% over 20 days, 11.4% below its 52-week high (~$26.3 in late July). Japanese bank shares sold off in October as domestic long yields fell and rebounded from Nov 9 (kabutan headlines 10/20, 10/23, 11/6, 11/9).

findings.finding: Q1 FY3/27 (Apr-Jun 2026) net income was ¥501.4bn, 29% of the unchanged ¥1.70tn FY guide, and net business profit was ¥722.3bn, 30% of the ¥2.40tn guide. The Q1 run-rate annualises to about ¥2.0tn before one-offs, and the street (~¥1.85tn) already sits above the guide. SMFG raised its FY guide at the interim in each of the last three years (2025: ¥1.3tn to ¥1.5tn), so a raise to roughly ¥1.85-1.95tn on 13 Nov is the central case. Q1 included ¥59.6bn of gains on cancelling investment trusts and ETF-sale gains of +¥46bn, so the clean run-rate is lower than the headline.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The ADR rose on all three recent interim guide raises: +5.6% on 2023-11-14, +2.9% on 2024-11-14 (¥1.06tn to ¥1.16tn) and +5.5% on 2025-11-14 (¥1.3tn to ¥1.5tn plus a ¥150bn buyback), per Yahoo daily closes. The Q1 beat with the guide unchanged (2026-07-31) moved +0.39%, then -2.43% the next session.
findings.why_not_priced: The raise itself is largely expected, since the consensus is ~9% above the guide. What is not priced is the size: a raise to ≥¥1.9tn would clear the street, while a token raise to ¥1.8tn would undershoot it. If the market had priced a large raise, the ADR would be near its July high ($26.3) and not 11% below its 52-week high after the October sell-off in bank shares.
findings.independence: Yahoo chart closes for the interim reaction history (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/SMFG?period1=1762300800&period2=1763251200&interval=1d). The 2025 interim raise is on kabutan (https://kabutan.jp/news/?b=k202511140660). Mizuho raised its FY net by ¥100bn as early as Q1, citing the June BOJ hike (https://pulse2.com/mizuho-raises-profit-outlook-%c2%a5100-billion-after-boj-rate-hike-and-doubles-buybacks-to-%c2%a5200-billion/).

findings.finding: The BOJ raised its policy rate to 1.25% on 2026-09-18, after the Q1 release. SMFG's FY3/27 plan assumes a 0.75% policy rate, and the company's own sensitivity is +¥110bn of NII in year 1 for every +25bp. It already counts +¥80bn in FY3/27 from the June hike to 1.0%, which is not in the ¥1.7tn target. Together the two hikes put roughly ¥130bn or more of pre-tax NII above the plan assumption for the fiscal year.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The same rate-driven line produced the 2025 interim raise (+5.5% ADR). Mizuho's Q1 raise on the June hike came with a doubled buyback.
findings.why_not_priced: Every sell-side model has the hike, so this is mostly priced into the consensus. What is not visible is whether SMFG puts the full Sept-hike NII into the revised FY guide, or keeps the buffer as it did at Q1, when it left the target unchanged despite the June hike. A raise carrying the full ¥130bn+ would sit above the ~¥1.85tn street figure.
findings.independence: The sensitivity (¥110bn year 1 per 25bp, plan assumption 0.75%) comes from SMFG's own 1Q deck (https://www.smfg.co.jp/english/investor/financial/latest_statement/2027_3/2027_1q_e03.pdf), the same document as finding 1, but here it is applied to a hike that came after that document. The BOJ hold at 1.25% on Oct 30 is confirmed separately (https://political.org/2026/10/29/bank-of-japan-holds-rates-at-1-25-but-speeds-up-sell-off-of-stock-holdings-capping-week-of-central-bank-surprises/).

findings.finding: Q1 total credit cost was ¥74.8bn against a ¥340bn FY guide (22%). The company said the 'anticipated negative impact of Middle East-related risks has not yet materialized', so the guide carries a buffer that could be cut at the interim.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No separate reaction history for the credit-cost line was found. It has been part of each interim raise.
findings.why_not_priced: Japanese banks usually keep credit buffers until the year end, so the street may not model a release at the interim. If it were priced, consensus credit cost would already be well below ¥340bn. That could not be verified, because there is no sourced line-item consensus.
findings.independence: Same document as findings 1 and 2. No other source for this point.

findings.finding: Capital return: SMFG's ¥100bn buyback set in May 2026 was completed by 2026-08-03, and it added no buyback at Q1. A year earlier it added ¥150bn at the interim, for ¥250bn in the year. Mizuho doubled its buyback to ¥200bn at Q1 2026. An interim buyback of about ¥150-200bn is therefore likely, and its size against the expected figure is a separate line on the 13 Nov release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-11-14: a ¥150bn interim buyback came with the guide raise and the ADR rose +5.5%. In May 2024, MUFG shares fell on a smaller-than-expected buyback (Bloomberg headline), so a small buyback is punished in this sector.
findings.why_not_priced: A buyback is expected, so the direction is mostly priced. A buyback of ¥200bn or more would beat the 2025 precedent, while one under ¥100bn would disappoint. Without a sourced street figure the sign is uncertain, which is why the range is wide.
findings.independence: The 2025 interim buyback (¥150bn, total ¥250bn) is in SMFG's 1H FY3/26 summary (https://www.smfg.co.jp/english/investor/financial/latest_statement/2026_3/2026_2q_e_summary.pdf). Mizuho's ¥200bn is on pulse2 (https://pulse2.com/mizuho-raises-profit-outlook-%c2%a5100-billion-after-boj-rate-hike-and-doubles-buybacks-to-%c2%a5200-billion/).

findings.finding: The bar is high and this name has not paid for beats without a guide change. The Q1 net beat (¥501.4bn against a Bloomberg consensus of about ¥429bn, +17%) with the guide unchanged moved the ADR +0.39% on 2026-07-31 and -2.43% the next session. The May 2026 initial guide of ¥1.7tn came in below a ¥1.761tn consensus and the ADR moved +1.0% on the day. With the street at ~¥1.85tn, a 1H beat alone, or a raise only to about ¥1.8tn, is likely to be sold.
findings.why_not_priced: This finding is about the reaction function, not about information. It sets the downside if the raise only meets the street.
findings.independence: The Q1 consensus beat is from the Bloomberg consensus as cited in https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/sumitomo-mitsui-financial-earnings-q1 / search snippet. The consensus above the guide is from Chartmill (snippet) and kabuyoho.

findings.finding: Domestic long-term yields fell in October and early November (10y JGB 2.78% on Oct 30, down 5.5bp that day) and Japanese bank shares sold off on it: kabutan headlines on 10/20 and 10/23 (Resona -7% intraday) and 11/6 (megabanks lower on risk-off bond buying), before a rebound on 11/9. The forward NII narrative and any bond-portfolio commentary at the interim will be read against this.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Sector sensitivity is high: Resona -7% intraday on 10/23 on the rate decline.
findings.why_not_priced: This is mostly priced already, through the ADR's -1.37% over 20 days. It is filed because management commentary on the December hike path (a Reuters poll had 54 of 78 economists expecting 1.5% this quarter) is a live line on the call.
findings.independence: The JGB level and the BOJ meeting are from political.org (https://political.org/2026/10/29/bank-of-japan-holds-rates-at-1-25-but-speeds-up-sell-off-of-stock-holdings-capping-week-of-central-bank-surprises/). This is a macro proxy.

findings.finding: FX: SMFG's FY3/27 plan assumes USD/JPY 150. The rate was 162.39 at end-June and about 156.7-157 after the 18 Sept BOJ hike, so overseas earnings translate above plan. FX added +¥25bn to Q1 net business profit.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None separately. For a USD-listed ADR a weaker yen partly offsets the earnings gain.
findings.why_not_priced: Standard analyst input, so mostly priced. This is a small, guide-supportive item.
findings.independence: The plan assumption and Q1 FX impact are from the SMFG 1Q deck (https://www.smfg.co.jp/english/investor/financial/latest_statement/2027_3/2027_1q_e03.pdf).

findings.finding: Jefferies (about 20% owned by SMFG, accounted for by the equity method) reported fiscal Q3 to 31 Aug 2026 net earnings to common of $260.6m against $224m a year earlier, with record investment banking. The Jul-Aug part of that falls in SMFG's 1H equity-method income, which is mildly positive, after the First Brands-related stress earlier in the year.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None for SMFG. Q1 equity-method income fell ¥25.1bn YoY on other items.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a counterparty print after SMFG last spoke, but it is small next to group net income of about ¥1.9tn.

findings.finding: On 2026-11-05 SMBC disclosed an information leakage after unauthorised access to a third-party email distribution service. It is a minor reputational item with no disclosed financial cost.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and small, so probably priced. It could come up in Q&A.

findings.finding: SMBC completed the sale of its SMBC MANUBANK commercial banking unit to Bank of Hope on 2026-10-01. That is after the 1H period end, but any gain or loss could be built into the revised FY guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Its size is unquantified and small relative to the group. Filed at zero.

baseline_tension: There is no usable skew and no crowded short. The 5-day run-up of +4% after an October sell-off is consistent with the market leaning toward the usual interim raise, so the findings mostly agree with what is expected and the edge lies only in the size of the raise and the buyback.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (verify the bar): the street consensus (~¥1.85tn) rests on a Chartmill snippet plus a scrambled kabuyoho table, so the main guidance finding was trimmed from +1.0 to +0.8
Rule 5 / two readings of one document: the BOJ-hike finding uses the same company sensitivity as the run-rate finding and both point to one guide raise, so it was trimmed from +0.6 to +0.5
Rule 5 (proxy): the FX finding is macro-to-company transmission and was trimmed from +0.2 to +0.15
History rule for foreign private issuers: the baseline's 6-K history was not used, and the base rate was rebuilt from confirmed release dates (this was done before reading the file; no change)
Rule 1 (fact is not a reaction): already reflected in the -0.4 positioning finding and in p_up 60; no further change, to avoid applying it twice
